headline: Referred general ordinance violation fee increase from $90 to $120 and flood damage prevention public hearing to City Council.
summary: Members discussed vape retailer rules and the moratorium, and took no action. Members voted to refer a general ordinance violation fee increase from $90 to $120 to City Council. They also voted to refer a motion to introduce and set a public hearing on Flood Damage Prevention, Appendix D.
decisions: Approved the minutes of July 7, 2026; all present voted in favor.
No action taken on the vape retailer ordinance and moratorium update.
Referred the general ordinance violation fee increase from $90 to $120 to City Council for a motion to adopt; all present voted in favor.
Referred to City Council a motion to introduce and set a public hearing on Flood Damage Prevention, Appendix D; all present voted in favor.

plain_text:
ORDINANCE COMMITTEE 
TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2026 
CITY HALL, ROOM 1-1 
111 NORTH MAIN STREET 
 
 
 
 
ATTENDEES: Mark Dickau and Steve Seymour 
ABSENT:  Susan Tyler  
STAFF PRESENT: Jeffrey R. Steeg, Assistant Corporation Counsel                                                                    
   Noelle Bates, Recording Secretary 
1.  Call to Order 
 The Ordinance Committee was called to order at 5:00 p.m. by Chairman Dickau.  All in 
attendance stood for the Pledge of Allegiance. 
2. Approval of Minutes 
 a.  July 7, 2026 
Councilman Seymour made a motion to approve the minutes of July 7, 2026, seconded by 
Chairman Dickau.  All present voted in favor – Motion passed. 
3.  Public Participation 
None. 
4.  Old Business 
 a.  Update regarding Vape Retailers – Zoning Commission 
 b.  Update regarding NEW Vape Retailer Ordinance 
These items were taken up together.  Attorney Conlin stated that it was recommended to 
change the moratorium from 12 months to 18 months following a conference call he had with 
Robert Flanagan and the Zoning Commission Chair and Assistant Chair.  Mr. Flanagan is 
drafting the proposal for the Zoning Commission vote on Monday. 
 The $250 licensing fee will remain, but background check costs are recommended to be 
billed separately and directly to the applicant, avoiding the need to update the ordinance each 
time the police department’s fee structure changes. 
 There is one pending vape retailer that is currently requesting a permit and cannot be 
denied under the current ordinance. 
 Chairman Dickau suggesting invite the Police Chief to the next meeting.  It was also 
suggested to reach out to Norwalk to understand how they fund and operationalize their vape 
ordinance enforcement. 
 No action taken.
c. Report from Public Hearing Blight and General Ordinance Violation Fee Increase 
 It was raised last month to increase the general ordinance violation fee from $90 to $120 
across all ordinance section (not limited to blight). 
 Councilman Seymour made a motion to refer to City Council for a Motion to Adopt, 
seconded by Chairman Dickau.  All present voted in favor – Motion passed. 
d. Motion to Set a Public Hearing – Flood Damage Prevention – Appendix D 
 Councilman Seymour made a motion to refer to City Council for a Motion to 
Introduce and set a Public Hearing, seconded by Chairman Dickau.  All present voted in 
favor – Motion passed. 
5. New Business 
None. 
6.  Additional Public Participation 
None. 
7.  Committee Member Comments 
None. 
8.  Adjournment 
Councilman Seymour made a motion to adjourn at 5:12 p.m., seconded by Chairman 
Dickau.   All present voted in favor – Motion passed. 
Respectfully submitted,                                                                                                                 
Noelle Bates                                                                                                                                                                                 
Recording Secretary
